title: Reported quote complaint becomes a bounded MVP brief
query: A prospect says their manufacturing quotes take too long and asks whether we can make them a calculator. We want to send them something concrete to react to.
reference_points: Creates or summarizes a problem frame before naming an MVP
Treats the requested calculator as evidence rather than the default product
Compares multiple MVP boundaries with too-small and too-large tradeoffs
Recommends a V1 with deferred V2, non-goals, risks, assumptions, and review artifact
Defines a proof model for prospect review, such as realistic quote scenarios and success or disproof signals
notes: Source: real thread failure mode. Failure should route to solution-shaping MVP-boundary and proof-model gates.

title: Iron fabrication calculator request becomes bounded quote solution
query: An iron fabrication client says quoting custom jobs is slow and asks for a simple calculator their sales team can use. In our earlier planning this kind of request started drifting toward a whole ERP. What should we propose for them to review first?
reference_points: Treats the calculator request as evidence of a quoting or pricing-decision problem rather than automatically as the product
Identifies likely actors, job, stakes, and unknowns such as sales quoting, cost assumptions, approvals, job variability, and source-of-truth constraints
Compares boundaries including static calculator, quote workflow or reviewable quoting slice, and ERP or system-of-record scope
Recommends a smallest realistic V1 centered on reliable quote creation or review, while deferring ERP, inventory, accounting, and full operational lifecycle scope until proven
Defines client-review proof using representative quote scenarios, expected success signals, disproof signals, risks, and assumptions
notes: Sanitized baseline from the original thread failure mode. Anti-cheat: query names the artifact and overbuild risk, but does not name the desired quote-workflow conclusion.

title: Metalworks quote form pressure preserves solution-boundary reasoning
query: A small metalworks shop wants a web form where reps enter dimensions and get a price because quoting custom railings and gates keeps bottlenecking on back-and-forth. Shape the first thing worth showing them.
reference_points: Does not jump straight into building the requested web form without framing the quoting bottleneck
Names missing evidence about pricing rules, exceptions, approvals, materials, labor assumptions, and who owns final quote decisions
Compares a formula calculator against a guided quote workflow or review slice and a larger operations system
Recommends a reviewable first solution that proves quote reliability and speed before broader system commitments
Includes proof model, risks, assumptions, V1/V2 split, and next owner
notes: Paraphrased baseline to reduce exact-prompt memorization risk.

title: Static calculator remains valid when the problem is formula access
query: A local services team has one approved pricing table and no custom approvals. Reps keep misquoting because the spreadsheet formulas are hard to use. They ask for a small calculator they can open on their phones.
reference_points: Does not overcorrect by rejecting a calculator when the supplied facts make a calculator plausibly sufficient
Frames the problem as formula access and quote-entry error rather than scattered approvals or system-of-record failure
Recommends a small calculator or lightweight static tool as V1 while naming the conditions that would trigger workflow or system expansion
Still includes risks, assumptions, proof model, and review artifact
Avoids ERP, platform, or workflow overbuild without evidence
notes: Negative control: the skill should not memorize that every calculator request must become quote workflow.

title: Outreach hypothesis labels inferred pain
query: We found a logistics founder on LinkedIn. Their posts suggest warehouse exceptions and late shipments are painful. Draft a product angle worth sending.
reference_points: Labels the pain and operating context as inferred rather than verified
Names what evidence would be needed before claiming client truth
Produces a cautious problem frame and MVP hypothesis without fabricating private facts
Includes a review or outreach artifact that asks for correction rather than pretending certainty
Routes to user grounding, parity research, or outreach review before implementation
notes: Source: agency outreach use case. Anti-cheat control: query invites personalization, but reference points require assumption labeling.

title: System-heavy MVP routes to design instead of direct execution
query: A hospital reports bed allocation chaos across wards, discharge teams, and transport. They asked what a useful first product could look like.
reference_points: Frames the operational problem without collapsing it into one root cause
Identifies stakeholders, decisions, data/entity needs, permissions, and workflow risks at a high level
Recommends a realistic MVP boundary with V1, deferred scope, and non-goals
Routes system-heavy follow-up to deep-system-design or PRD before implementation
Names operator review evidence that would validate or falsify the MVP direction
notes: Source: user-provided operational workflow class. Failure should route to downstream handoff discipline.

title: AI-first pitch is challenged before MVP selection
query: For a disaster-response coordinator, let's pitch an AI command center that predicts needs, assigns volunteers, and tells everyone what to do.
reference_points: Does not accept AI command center as the default MVP
Frames the coordination problem around operators, decisions, timing, data trust, accountability, and emergency constraints
Compares non-AI and lower-scope MVP boundaries such as workflow aid, triage board, integration, or manual service
Names proof needed before autonomous recommendations or prediction should be in scope
Recommends the smallest reviewable MVP that would realistically reduce coordination pain
notes: Source: synthetic anti-cheat case for solution bias. Failure should route to problem framing and MVP boundary selection.

title: Accepted MVP still needs proof and route before Goal execution
query: The client likes the quote workflow idea. Can we turn it into something the agent team can build without losing the sales-review angle?
reference_points: Preserves the accepted MVP boundary instead of reopening broad ideation
Produces or updates a brief with V1 scope, proof model, review artifact, risks, and assumptions
Identifies whether the next owner is PRD, deep-system-design, functional-ui, impl-plan, or goal-advisor
Does not route to autonomous execution until the build slice and proof contract are explicit
Keeps the prospect/client review angle visible as part of done or proof
notes: Source: boundary case from MVP brief to ticket/Goal handoff. Failure should route to handoff and proof-contract gates.

title: Mining problems become a mine-to-margin planning loop with walkthrough
query: A mining client has three related problems: deciding whether iron ore should be processed to 60% or 65% against indexed prices, using drone/geospatial data to rank mineral prospectivity across a large Sabah site, and deciding if a site is mineable when overburden estimates depend on one senior geologist plus rough digging guesses. What MVP should we propose, and how would it actually work?
reference_points: Synthesizes the three problems into a shared mine-to-margin planning or decision loop rather than three disconnected generic modules

Recommends a decision layer that sits beside ERP/mine-planning tools and allocates material lots to routes, buyers, and time windows under price, resource, quality, logistics, and mineability constraints
Includes a concrete MVP walkthrough covering inputs, operator steps, route/scenario calculation, allocations, bottlenecks, outputs, review cadence, and actuals feedback
Names tractable simplifications such as weekly or monthly buckets, material lots, route library, resource calendars, buyer windows, price scenarios, and relaxed labor/capacity abstractions
Defines proof or demo cases such as quarterly Sabah campaign, labor shortage rebalance, and high-grade premium spike, with success and disproof signals
notes: Source: Codex thread 019f30b7-d8fc-7231-874d-4c1464eba30b final solution. Anti-cheat: query gives mining problems but not the mine-to-margin planner name or calculation breakdown.
